results.goal: How did order revenue and volume develop over 2024–2025, and how much does order value differ by region and by the number of units sold?
results.reading: This is an order-level sales file of 300 orders placed between January 2024 and December 2025, with one row per order. Each row records the order date, the sales region it belongs to, the revenue the order brought in, and how many units it contained. The dates span 24 months (267 distinct dates), so the grain is a single transaction rather than a monthly or regional total. Revenue is a continuous money amount while units is a bounded integer count.
quality_risks: No currency is stated anywhere in the file; all revenue figures are assumed to be in one consistent currency.
Only 24 months and 2 calendar years are covered, so long-run trends, multi-year extremes and seasonality beyond two cycles cannot be established.
Every revenue value is distinct (300 distinct of 300 rows), so this is raw order grain — mixing it with monthly or regional totals would double-count.
Revenue is right-skewed with a long tail of large orders, so a few big transactions can move regional averages; medians are safer.
With only region, date and units as context, nothing separates product mix, customer type or discounting from a genuine regional difference.
Units top out at 40 and are integers, which may indicate a capped or binned field rather than an exact item count.
plan_applied: kept the 4 columns the goal needs, set aside 2 others

analyses.title: revenue by region
analyses.sentence: By region, the highest average revenue is North (1,034, 95% range 917 to 1,158, 75 rows) and the lowest West (840, 77 rows): a gap of 194 (95% range 17.3 to 387).
analyses.method: Each group's average with a 95% bootstrap range (999 resamples); groups with fewer than 5 values are left out. An association with the group, not its cause.

analyses.title: units and revenue
analyses.sentence: Across 300 rows, higher units goes with higher revenue, strongly (Spearman 0.976, 95% range 0.969 to 0.981). An association, not a cause.
analyses.method: Spearman rank correlation (it reads any steady rise or fall, not only a straight line); 95% range by the Fisher transform with the Spearman correction.

analyses.title: How revenue is spread
analyses.sentence: revenue: half the 300 values lie between 476 and 1,370 (median 926); one in ten is below 208 and one in ten above 1,664.
analyses.method: Percentiles of every value; the bars count values in equal-width bins.

analyses.title: Largest revenue by region in 2025
analyses.sentence: In 2025 the largest yearly total revenue by region were East (44,617), North (42,350), South (32,738); together 78.6% of the total over all 4 region entries.
analyses.method: Each region entry's yearly total (every row added) for each complete calendar year; the latest year at least 80% of the entries report. Dates from the order_date column.

analyses.title: What predicts revenue
analyses.sentence: A straight-line model of revenue from units, region, trained on earlier dates and scored on the 4 later blocks, predicts them with R squared 0.949 and a typical error of 91.1, against 475 for the mean of its training rows. units carries most of it (R squared falls by 0.949 without it). An association the model learned, not a cause.
